Title: Flight 15 pairing undergo testing at Massey’s
Author: Eleanor Day and Chris Bergin
Date: September 9, 2026
Outlet: NASASpaceFlight.com
URL: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/09/flight-15-pairing-masseys/

SpaceX has rolled Super Heavy Booster 22 out of Mega Bay 1 to Massey’s for cryogenic proof testing. Ship 42 has since joined it there on its second trip to the test site. The pair is slated to fly on Flight 15, which could come about a month after the upcoming Flight 14 if that mission goes well.

Ship 42 completed two cryogenic campaigns at Massey’s on the ship cryo stand a few days before B22 rolled. However, it was rolled back out to the test site for what is likely another round of cryo testing.

These tests confirm structural integrity and put the vehicle under the thermal and pressure loads it sees before and during flight. Teams typically load liquid oxygen into the LOX tanks at full or partial fill and use liquid nitrogen in the methane tanks. The ship then holds for several hours while temperatures, pressures, COPVs, and strain gauges are monitored.

Once Ship 42 has completed this phase of testing, engine installation is the next major step toward launch.
